findings: The standalone probe preserves parsed shader operations while clearing only the bytecode identity that selects the shipping 512-lane cap. It tests 988-, 1008- and 1061-word captured shaders at 512, 1024, 2048 and 4096 lanes, with both point and linear sampling and six constant/coordinate scenarios. Every output component is compared to an independent scalar shader interpreter.

Both runtimes pass all 12 CPU cases. The old runtime passes all three 512-lane NPU cases, but rejects every larger NPU batch during Intel compiler layout legalization. These are actual compilation attempts, not policy rejections.

The candidate runtime rejects all 12 NPU attempts before compilation because precise_0 does not survive the existing round-trip assertion. Therefore no candidate NPU batch compilation or arithmetic result is established. A compatibility investigation is required; removing the assertion alone would not qualify precision.
The candidate is isolated under toolchains/openvino-2026.4.1. The baseline environment and physical driver are unchanged. No live desktop stream or CPU build overlaps the comparison.

sources.finding: Subsequent source inspection shows IR normalization migrates the legacy marker to DisablePrecisionConversion; the original key-presence assertion does not recognize this migration.
The replacement attribute visits a value string representing its source-to-target map, allowing independent inspection through public runtime attribute visitors.
